The Prime Sieve as a Stack of Orthogonal Periodic Fields: Density, Entropy, Spectrum
The Multiplier Set of a Prime
The Orthogonal Stream Prime Generator: A Complete Algorithm
Algorithm C — the min-factor exponent-spine generator
Factorization from the Orthogonal Stream Family
Twin Primes in the Wheel Lattice

nodes.name: Ownership by Smallest Prime Factor
nodes.statement: A composite m is owned by the prime p exactly when p is the smallest prime factor of m; the owned set is Θ_p = { m composite : spf(m) = p }.

sources.heading: 2.4 Orthogonal Streams
sources.quote: A composite number \(m\) is **owned** by the prime \(p\) if \(p\) is the smallest prime factor of \(m\).

sources.heading: 2.1 The partition
sources.quote: Write `spf(m)` for the smallest prime factor of `m > 1`.

sources.heading: T10
sources.quote: A composite \(m\) is **owned** by \(p = \mathrm{spf}(m)\).

nodes.name: p-Rough Numbers
nodes.statement: An integer m is p-rough when no prime smaller than p divides it, equivalently when gcd(m, P_{<p}) = 1 for the primorial P_{<p} of the primes below p.

sources.heading: 1. Notation
sources.quote: \(R_p = \{m\ge 1 : \gcd(m,P_{<p})=1\}\) the \(p\)-**rough** numbers: no prime factor \(< p\)
call `m` **`p`-rough** if no prime `< p` divides it, equivalently `gcd(m, P_{<p}) = 1`

nodes.name: Multiplier Set A_p
nodes.statement: The multiplier set of a prime p is A_p = { a ≥ p : gcd(a, P_{<p}) = 1 }, the p-rough numbers from p upward.

sources.heading: Overview
sources.quote: \Theta_N = N \cdot A_N, \qquad A_N = \{ a \ge N : \gcd(a, P_{<N}) = 1 \}
A_p = R_p \cap [p,\infty)

nodes.name: Stage-k Wheel Lattice S_k
nodes.statement: The stage-k lattice is S_k = { r mod P_k : gcd(r, P_k) = 1 }, the residues surviving the first k periodic exclusion fields, of size φ(P_k) and density κ_k = φ(P_k)/P_k.

sources.heading: 1. The lattice
sources.quote: S_k = { r mod P_k : gcd(r, P_k) = 1 } the **stage-\(k\) lattice**
`S_k` is exactly the wheel of §4.2 at `W = P_k`.

nodes.name: Multiplier Cloud B_p
nodes.statement: B_p is the multiplicative monoid generated by the primes greater than p, i.e. B_p = { r ≥ 1 : every prime divisor of r exceeds p } = { r : gcd(r, P_{≤p}) = 1 }.
nodes.formal: B_p = \{ r \ge 1 : q \mid r \Rightarrow q > p \}

sources.heading: 1. Notation
sources.quote: B_p = { r ≥ 1 : q prime, q ∣ r ⟹ q > p } the monoid generated by the primes > p
Write \(B_p = \{ r \ge 1 : q \text{ prime},\ q \mid r \Rightarrow q > p \}\)

nodes.name: Layer (p, e)
nodes.statement: A layer (p, e) is the stream p^e · B̃_p of integers whose smallest prime factor is p with p-adic valuation e, where B̃_p = {1} ∪ { r ≥ p : gcd(r, W) = 1, p ∤ r } is the wheeled relaxation of B_p.

sources.heading: 4C.1
sources.quote: let layer `(p, e)` be the stream `p^e·B̃_p`, minus the single non-composite element `p`

nodes.name: NextRough Successor
nodes.statement: NextRough(p, y) denotes the least p-rough integer strictly greater than y; it is the successor function on the wheel of modulus P_{<p}.

sources.quote: Define \(\mathrm{NextRough}(p,y) = \min\{a \in R_p : a > y\}\)

sources.heading: T28
sources.quote: \(\mathrm{NextRough}(p,\cdot)\) is the successor function on the wheel of modulus \(P_{<p}\).

nodes.name: NextOwnedComposite Primitive
nodes.statement: NextOwnedComposite(p, x) is the least element of Θ_p strictly greater than x, the single per-prime advance primitive of the architecture.

sources.heading: 3.1 Definition
sources.quote: \text{NextOwnedComposite}(p, x) = \min\{ m \in \Theta_p : m > x \}

sources.heading: T26
sources.quote: \(\mathrm{NOC}(p, x) = \min\{ m \in \Theta_p : m > x \}\).

nodes.name: Claimant Set of a Composite
nodes.statement: The claimant set of a W-coprime composite m under Algorithm B is claimants_B(m) = { p prime : p ∣ m and p² ≤ m }, the set of streams that pop m.

sources.quote: the set of streams that claim `m` is exactly `{ p prime : p ∣ m, p² ≤ m }`

sources.heading: 2. Notation
sources.quote: `claimants_B(m)` | `{ p prime : p ∣ m, p² ≤ m }` (`AlgB.claims_iff`)

nodes.name: Pair Lattice S_k^{(2)}
nodes.statement: The pair lattice is S_k^{(2)} = { r mod P_k : gcd(r(r+2), P_k) = 1 }, the twin-candidate residue classes modulo the k-th primorial, of size T_k and density τ_k = T_k / P_k.

sources.heading: 1. Notation
sources.quote: `S_k^{(2)}` | the **pair lattice**: `{ r mod P_k : gcd(r(r+2), P_k) = 1 }`

nodes.name: Periodic Exclusion Field of a Prime
nodes.statement: Each prime p emits the period-p mask M_p(n) which is 0 when p divides n and 1 otherwise; the partial sieve S_k is the pointwise product of the first k such masks.

sources.heading: 2.1 The single-prime field
sources.quote: For a prime \(p\), define the periodic mask ... This is a period-\(p\) function on \(\mathbb{Z}\)

sources.heading: What You Are Looking At
sources.quote: every prime p emits a perfectly periodic exclusion field M_p that kills exactly the multiples of p

nodes.name: Square-Root Divisor Bound
nodes.statement: Every composite m with 2 ≤ m ≤ N² has a prime factor p ≤ N, so the primes up to N form a complete divisor basis for the band up to N².
nodes.formal: m = ab,\ 1 < a \le b \Rightarrow a^2 \le m \le N^2 \Rightarrow a \le N

sources.quote: **Lemma 1.** Let \(m\) be composite with \(2 \le m \le N^2\). Then \(m\) has a prime factor \(p \le N\).

sources.heading: T2
sources.quote: If \(m\) is composite and \(2 \le m \le N^2\), then \(m\) has a prime factor \(p \le N\).

nodes.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem for Primorial Moduli
nodes.statement: For distinct primes p_1..p_k with L_k = ∏ p_i, the ring Z/L_kZ is isomorphic to the product of the Z/p_iZ, so each residue is an independent tuple of per-prime coordinates.

sources.heading: 2.4 CRT reading
sources.quote: \mathbb{Z}/L_k\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/p_1\mathbb{Z} \times \cdots \times \mathbb{Z}/p_k\mathbb{Z}

sources.heading: T4
sources.quote: For distinct primes \(p_1,\dots,p_k\) with \(L_k = \prod p_i\), \(\mathbb{Z}/L_k\mathbb{Z} \cong \prod_i \mathbb{Z}/p_i\mathbb{Z}\).

nodes.name: Primorial Growth Is Exponential in p_k
nodes.statement: The primorial satisfies P_k = e^{(1+o(1))p_k}, so any construction whose storage or period is P_k becomes infeasible past p_k ≈ 40–60.

sources.heading: T5
sources.quote: any construction whose storage or period is \(P_k\) is infeasible past \(p_k \approx 40\text{–}60\)

nodes.name: Mertens' Third Theorem
nodes.statement: The product ∏_{p ≤ y}(1 − 1/p) is asymptotic to e^{−γ}/log y, so wheel density thins only logarithmically while the wheel period grows exponentially.

sources.heading: T7
sources.quote: the wheel modulo \(P_k\) thins only *logarithmically* while its period grows *exponentially*

nodes.name: Jacobsthal Gap Bounds for Primorials
nodes.statement: The maximal gap g(P_k) between consecutive integers coprime to P_k satisfies g(P_k) ≪ log² P_k and g(P_k) ≫ p_k log p_k log log log p_k / (log log p_k)², so scanning for the next rough number is superlinear in p in the worst case.

sources.heading: T9
sources.quote: \(g(P_k) \ll \log^2 P_k \asymp p_k^2\) (Iwaniec), and \(g(P_k) \gg p_k \log p_k \log\log\log p_k/(\log\log p_k)^2\)

nodes.name: Buchstab Count of Rough Numbers
nodes.statement: The count Φ(x, y) of y-rough integers up to x satisfies Φ(x, y) ~ ω(u)·x/log y with u = log x / log y and ω the Buchstab function; hence stream p fires about ω(u)X/(p log p) times below X.

sources.heading: T8
sources.quote: \(\Phi(x,y) \sim \omega(u)\,x/\log y\) with \(u = \log x/\log y\), \(\omega\) the Buchstab function
asymptotically `≈ ω(u)·X/(p log p)` with Buchstab `ω`

nodes.name: Ownership Theorem: Θ_p = p · A_p
nodes.statement: For every prime p the owned composites are exactly Θ_p = p·A_p with A_p the p-rough numbers from p up, the map a ↦ pa is a bijection A_p → Θ_p, and the family {Θ_p} partitions the composites.

sources.heading: 2.1 Ownership theorem
sources.quote: **Theorem 2.1 (multiplier set).** For every prime \(p\), \Theta_p = p \cdot A_p
_Status: **machine-checked** — `Primegen.theta_eq_image`

sources.heading: 1. Statement
sources.quote: \(\Theta_N\) is exactly the set of composites whose smallest prime factor is \(N\)

nodes.name: A_p Is a Wheel, Not a Prime List
nodes.statement: Membership in A_p depends only on a mod P_{<p}, so A_p ∪ {1} is periodic modulo P_{<p} with φ(P_{<p}) = ∏_{q<p}(q−1) residues per period, and A_p is infinite.

sources.quote: **Corollary 2.2.** \(A_p \cup \{1\}\) is periodic modulo \(P_{<p}\) with \(\varphi(P_{<p})\) residues per period
\(A_N\) is **infinite**, and the finite list above is one period, not the whole set

nodes.name: Phase Separation
nodes.statement: If a ∈ A_p and a < p² then a is prime, so the multipliers of p below p² are exactly the primes in [p, p²) and advancing a stream there is a single index increment into the prime array.
nodes.formal: a \in A_p,\ a < p^2 \Rightarrow a \text{ prime}

sources.quote: **Lemma 2.3 (phase separation).** If \(a \in A_p\) and \(a < p^2\), then \(a\) is prime.
**Claim O2 (phase separation).** If `a ∈ A_p` and `a < p²` then `a` is prime.

nodes.name: First Owned Composite Is p²
nodes.statement: The least element of Θ_p is p², always and not merely typically, because the least admissible multiplier is p itself.

sources.quote: **Corollary.** \(\min \Theta_p = p^2\) — always, not "typically"

sources.heading: T12a
sources.quote: it is not "typically", it is **always**

nodes.name: One Period Is '1 Plus Primes' Exactly for p ≤ 7
nodes.statement: One period of A_p consists of 1 together with primes only when P_{<p} ≤ p², which holds precisely for p ∈ {2,3,5,7}; the first composite multiplier anywhere is 121 = 11², giving 11·121 = 11³ ∈ Θ_11.

sources.quote: The first composite multiplier anywhere is \(121 = 11^2\)

nodes.name: The Advance Primitive Is Exactly a Wheel Successor
nodes.statement: NextOwnedComposite(p, x) equals p · NextRough(p, max(p−1, ⌊x/p⌋)), so the generator is a merge of wheel successor functions and there is no further primitive to discover.

sources.quote: **Proposition 2.6.** ... \mathrm{NextOwnedComposite}(p,x) = p \cdot \mathrm{NextRough}(p, \max(p-1, \lfloor x/p \rfloor))
There is no other formula to find: _the generator is a merge of wheel successor functions._

nodes.name: Causality: No Forward Dependence
nodes.statement: If all primes below n are known, the scan is at n and n = pa ∈ Θ_p, then a ≤ n/2 and the next multiplier a' = NextRough(p, a) satisfies a' < n, so no step ever consults an integer ≥ n and the generator is self-hosting.

sources.quote: **Theorem 2.8 (causality).** ... (iii) \(a'\) is determined by data about integers \(< n\) only.
no step ever consults an integer \(\ge n\)

nodes.name: No O(1)-Time, Polylog-Space NextRough (Conjecture X1)
nodes.statement: No algorithm computes NextRough(p, y) in O(1) time and poly(log p, log y) space given only the primes below p, because an exact per-prime wheel table has e^{(1+o(1))p} entries and any stateless alternative is trial division.

sources.quote: **Conjecture X1 (obstruction).** There is no algorithm computing `NextRough(p, y)` in O(1) time and `poly(log p, log y)` space

sources.heading: T31
sources.quote: **This should be labelled a conjecture, not an assumption.**

nodes.name: Stream Tree Partition (Claim A1)
nodes.statement: For b ≥ 2 the streams Σ_b = { b·q : q prime, q ≥ P(b) } partition the composites, each is increasing, and its successor operation is advancing one index in the prime array.

sources.quote: **Theorem 3.1 (stream tree).** ... Then \(\{\Sigma_b\}_{b\ge 2}\) is a partition of the composites
_Status: **machine-checked** — `AlgA.exists_unique_split`

nodes.name: Algorithm A — Exact One-Touch Orthogonal Generator
nodes.statement: Algorithm A generates primes by merging the exact stream tree with lazy child creation, using EMIT and SPAWN cursors, no marking array, no divisibility test, and exactly one queue pop per composite.

sources.heading: 3. Algorithm A
sources.quote: **Algorithm A** (§3) pays in _streams_: perfectly orthogonal, **each composite touched exactly once**
Algorithm A is included because it realises the partition of §2.1 with zero redundancy

nodes.name: Algorithm A Correctness
nodes.statement: Algorithm A emits precisely the primes ≤ N in increasing order and pops exactly one queue record per composite in [4, N].
nodes.notes: Proved by induction in algorithm.md §3.5; paper.md marks the same claim A2 as TODO, so status is 'proposed' rather than 'accepted'.

sources.quote: **Theorem 3.2 (correctness).** `A(N)` emits precisely the primes \(\le N\), in increasing order
**Claim A2 (correctness).** ... _TODO: induction on `n` using Claim A1_

nodes.name: Algorithm A Array Accesses Are Legal
nodes.statement: Every prime-array access performed while Algorithm A processes n reads an entry strictly smaller than n, by Bertrand's postulate applied in the EMIT and SPAWN branches.

sources.quote: **Theorem 3.5 (causality, Algorithm A).** Every array access `primes[j]` performed while processing \(n\) satisfies `primes[j] < n`

nodes.name: Algorithm A Live-Stream Count Is N^0.75
nodes.statement: The number of simultaneously live streams S(N) = π(√N) + #{ b ≥ 2 : b·P(b) ≤ N } grows as N^{θ+o(1)} with θ ≈ 0.75.

sources.quote: **Conjecture A4.** `S(N) = N^{θ+o(1)}` with `θ ≈ 0.75`.
maximises near \(\beta \approx 0.6\) and gives \(S(N) = N^{\theta+o(1)}\) with \(\theta \approx 0.75\)

nodes.name: Dickman Saddle-Point Estimate for S(N)
nodes.statement: A saddle-point estimate using Dickman's ρ, counting bases of size N^β against primes up to N^{(1−β)/2}, maximises near β ≈ 0.6 and yields the exponent θ ≈ 0.75 for the live-stream count.

sources.quote: A saddle-point estimate using Dickman's \(\rho\) ... Measure it with the `stats` mode ... before trusting the exponent.

nodes.name: Algorithm A + Wheel Variant
nodes.statement: Variant A+wheel fixes W = p_1···p_w, emits the small primes directly, steps only over W-coprime candidates and builds bases only from primes greater than p_w, suppressing the smooth bases that dominate S(N) while preserving one-touch behaviour.

sources.quote: the reduction is large (empirically an order of magnitude at \(w=6\)) though we do not attempt a sharp exponent

nodes.name: Algorithm B — Wheeled Streaming Generator
nodes.statement: Algorithm B fixes a wheel modulus W, scans only W-coprime candidates, replaces each exact multiplier set A_p by the shared relaxation Ã_p = { a ≥ p : gcd(a,W) = 1 }, and advances each stream with one table lookup and one multiply.

sources.heading: 4. Algorithm B
sources.quote: This is the recommended construction.

sources.heading: 4.1 Design
sources.quote: Advancement is exact O(1) with O(1) state: `a += step[a % W]`, `v = p*a`.

nodes.name: Algorithm B Coverage
nodes.statement: Every W-coprime composite m has spf(m) > p_w, quotient a = m/p that is W-coprime with a ≥ p, hence m is a value of the stream of p.

sources.quote: **Lemma 4.1 (coverage).** ... \(m = p\cdot a\) with \(a\in\tilde A_p\): \(m\) is a value of the stream of \(p\).
_Status: **machine-checked** — `AlgB.coverage`

nodes.name: Algorithm B Makes No Early Claims
nodes.statement: Every key in Algorithm B's queue is at least the scan position n and is a W-coprime composite at least p² for its owning prime, because heads p² are inserted exactly when n reaches p² and advancement strictly increases the key.

sources.quote: **Lemma 4.2 (no early claims).** Every key in \(Q\) is \(\ge n\)
the `ahead` field of `AlgB.Inv` is preserved by `AlgB.inv_step`

nodes.name: Algorithm B Emits Exactly the Primes
nodes.statement: Algorithm B emits exactly the primes in increasing order forever; a W-coprime candidate is prime if and only if no queue key equals it.

attributes.value: per-candidate decision machine-checked; outer induction open

sources.quote: **Theorem 4.3.** `B()` emits exactly the primes, in increasing order, forever.
The outer induction "the emitted prefix is exactly the primes below `n`" is not yet formalised

nodes.name: Algorithm B Has O(1) State Per Prime
nodes.statement: Advancement in Algorithm B performs no prime lookups at all and activation reads only primes[act] with primes[act] ≤ √n, so the generator is a genuine online stream carrying two words per prime.

sources.quote: **Theorem 4.4 (state).** Advancement uses no prime lookups at all
`AlgB.Rec` carries exactly `(p, a)`, two words

nodes.name: Algorithm B Duplicate Accounting
nodes.statement: A W-coprime composite m is popped once for each prime factor p of m with p_w < p ≤ √m, so total queue operations to N are approximately κ_W·N·(ln ln √N − ln ln p_w).

attributes.value: claimant identity machine-checked; the sum is a measurement

sources.quote: \mathrm{ops}(N) \approx \kappa_W N(\ln\ln\sqrt N - \ln\ln p_w + o(1))
the set of streams that claim `m` is exactly `{ p prime : p ∣ m, p² ≤ m }`

nodes.name: Algorithm B Touch Factor at N = 10^12
nodes.statement: At w = 6 and N = 10^12 the duplicate accounting gives ops ≈ 0.46·N against the one-touch ideal ≈ 0.19·N, a factor of about 2.4 more touches, in exchange for 78,498 records instead of about 10^9.

sources.quote: \(\mathrm{ops} \approx 0.46\,N\) — versus the one-touch ideal \(\kappa_W N - \pi(N) \approx 0.19\,N\)

nodes.name: Algorithm B Supports O(1) Segment Restart
nodes.statement: For a segment beginning at X the state of stream p is recomputed in O(1) as a_0 = max(p, next_coprime_ge(⌈X/p⌉)) with value p·a_0, so segments are independent and the generator parallelises like a segmented sieve.

sources.quote: **Random-access restart (parallelism):** for a segment beginning at \(X\), the state of stream \(p\) is recomputed in O(1)

nodes.name: Deferred Activation Bounds the Queue at π(√n)
nodes.statement: Because a prime contributes nothing below p², inserting its stream only when the scan reaches p² keeps the queue at π(√n) records forever, with no global limit and no pre-pass.

sources.quote: inserting its stream only at `n = p²` keeps the queue at `π(√n)` records forever

sources.heading: T38
sources.quote: the heap holds only \(\pi(\sqrt{n})\) entries

nodes.name: Min-Factor Normal Form (Claim M1)
nodes.statement: Every integer n > 1 factors uniquely as n = p^e·r with p prime, e ≥ 1 and r ∈ B_p, and then necessarily p = spf(n), e = v_p(n), r = n/p^e; hence Θ_p is the disjoint union of the layers p^e·B_p minus {p}.
nodes.formal: n = p^{e} r,\ p = \mathrm{spf}(n),\ e = v_p(n),\ r \in B_p

sources.quote: **Claim M1 (min-factor normal form).** Every integer `n > 1` factors **uniquely** as n = p^e · r
**Theorem 2.10 (min-factor normal form).** Every \(n>1\) is **uniquely** \(n = p^{e} r\)

nodes.name: Cone Recursion for B_p (Claim M2, as printed)
nodes.statement: As originally printed, B_p = {1} ⊎ ⨄_{q>p prime} q·B_q, expressing the multiplier cloud of p as generated by the clouds of the larger primes so that coprimality is emergent rather than tested.
nodes.notes: Retained because the notes retain it: the printed identity is false and is superseded by Correction M2'.

sources.quote: **Claim M2 (cone recursion).** For every prime `p`, B_p = {1} ⊎ ⨄_{q > p prime} q · B_q .
**Proposition 2.11 (cone recursion).** \(B_p = \{1\} \uplus \biguplus_{q>p} q\cdot B_q\).

nodes.name: Correction M2′ — Run-Length and One-Step Cone Forms
nodes.statement: The printed cone recursion is false, with least witness 9 ∈ B_2 lying in no q·B_q; the correct forms are B_p = {1} ⊎ ⨄_{q>p} ⨄_{e≥1} q^e·B_q (run-length) and B_p = {1} ⊎ ⨄_{q>p} q·{ s : spf(s) ≥ q } (one-step).

sources.quote: **Correction M2′ (forced by the formalisation).** The displayed identity is **false as written**

nodes.name: Strict Phase Separation in a Layer (Claim M3)
nodes.statement: If r ∈ B_p and 1 < r < (p+1)² then r is prime, so a composite multiplier in layer (p,e) forces the emitted value to be at least p^{e+2} and layer e has a rough phase below N only for p ≤ N^{1/(e+2)}.

sources.quote: **Claim M3.** If `r ∈ B_p` and `1 < r < (p+1)²` then `r` is prime
**Lemma 2.12 (strict phase separation).**

nodes.name: Causality for Layers (Claim M4)
nodes.statement: For a layer value m = p^e·r with r > 1, the next admissible multiplier r' satisfies r ≤ m/p and r' < m, so Algorithm C is realisable online with a wider margin than Algorithm B.

sources.quote: **Claim M4 (causality).** ... `r ≤ m/p ≤ m/2` and `r' < m`

nodes.name: Algorithm C — Min-Factor Exponent-Spine Generator
nodes.statement: Algorithm C is Algorithm B re-indexed by the min-factor normal form: streams are layers (p, e) with a spine of pure powers and a wheeled cloud, advanced by a wheel step plus a skip cursor that enforces p ∤ r.

sources.heading: 5. Specification
sources.quote: Algorithm C is Algorithm B re-indexed by Claim M1: streams are **layers** `(p, e)` rather than primes `p`.

sources.heading: 4C
sources.quote: It is a streaming min-factor oracle, not a faster prime generator.

nodes.name: Algorithm C Coverage (M6)
nodes.statement: Every W-coprime composite m is a value of layer (p, e) with p = spf(m) and e = v_p(m).

sources.quote: **Claim M6 (coverage).** Every `W`-coprime composite `m` is a value of layer `(p, e)`

nodes.name: Algorithm C Soundness (M7)
nodes.statement: Every key in Algorithm C's queue is a W-coprime composite, so a prime candidate can never be claimed.

sources.quote: **Claim M7 (soundness).** Every key in `Q` is a `W`-coprime composite.

nodes.name: Algorithm C No Early Claims (M8)
nodes.statement: Every key in Algorithm C's queue is at least the scan position and at least p² for its owning prime.
nodes.notes: Only the p² half is machine-checked (MinFac.sq_le_of_claims); the ≥ n half is the unformalised loop invariant.

sources.quote: 🟡 the `≥ p²` half only; the `≥ n` half is the loop invariant

nodes.name: Algorithm C Decision Rule (M9)
nodes.statement: A W-coprime candidate is prime if and only if no key equals it, and Algorithm C emits exactly the primes in increasing order forever.

sources.quote: **Claim M9 (decision rule).** ... `C()` emits exactly the primes, in increasing order, forever.

nodes.name: Algorithm C Claimants Are a Strict Subset of B's (M10)
nodes.statement: claimants_C(m) = { (p, v_p(m)) : p ∣ m and (m = p^{v_p} or m/p^{v_p} ≥ p) } is contained in claimants_B(m), one layer per claiming prime, and the inclusion is strict.

sources.quote: **Claim M10 (duplicate accounting).** ... claimants_C(m) ⊆ claimants_B(m)

nodes.name: Streaming Min-Factor Oracle (M11)
nodes.statement: The drained claimant with the smallest p carries (spf(n), v_p(n), n/p^{v_p}), so Algorithm C reports the min-factor normal form of every rejected candidate at no cost beyond the drain.

sources.quote: **Claim M11 (streaming min-factor oracle).** ... that record's `(p, e, r)` satisfies `p = spf(n)`

nodes.name: 847 = 7·11² Separates B's and C's Claimant Sets
nodes.statement: At W = 30 the composite 847 = 7·11² is claimed twice by Algorithm B (as 7·121 and 11·77) and once by Algorithm C (layer (7,1) with r = 121), the smallest strict witness for the claimant inclusion.

sources.quote: m = 847 = 7 · 11²  :   B claims twice ... C claims once
Least witness at `W = 30`: `m = 847 = 7·11²`

nodes.name: Algorithm C Saves Only Θ(N^{2/3}/log N) Touches
nodes.statement: Algorithm C's touch count equals Algorithm B's leading term minus Θ(N^{2/3}/log N); at N = 10^12 and w = 6 that gap is about 10^{-4}·N against ops_B ≈ 0.46·N, so C is not a faster prime generator.

sources.quote: **Algorithm C is not a faster prime generator.**

sources.heading: 4C.3
sources.quote: that gap is `≈10⁻⁴·N` against `ops_B ≈ 0.46·N`

nodes.name: Thinned Spine Restores π(√n) Memory for Algorithm C
nodes.statement: Handling n = p² inline at activation and gating higher spine elements on a second activation cursor over primes with p³ ≤ n reduces Algorithm C's record count to (1+o(1))·π(√n).

sources.quote: records_C(n) = π(√n) + O( π(n^{1/3})·log n / log p )  =  (1 + o(1))·π(√n)

nodes.name: Algorithm C∞ — Exact Layer Form
nodes.statement: Algorithm C∞ streams each exact layer p^e·B_p with B_p supplied by the cone recursion; it is one-touch but is Algorithm A read in the opposite orientation and is not segment-restartable.

sources.quote: **Claim M5.** Algorithm C∞ is Algorithm A read in the opposite orientation

nodes.name: The Stream Family Cannot Factor a Single Target (FC0)
nodes.statement: Determining spf(N) for a single input N by running any member of the stream family costs Ω(π(√N)) in the best case and Ω(κ_W·N) if run as specified, because factorization is the transpose of generation and the architecture has no locality in that direction.

sources.heading: 1. Scope
sources.quote: **Claim FC0 (the no-go).** ... costs `Ω(π(√N))` operations in the best case

nodes.name: Algorithm B's Drain Knows All But One Prime Factor (FC-B1)
nodes.statement: For a W-coprime composite m the prime divisors are claimants_B(m) together with the large part L(m), which is 1 or a single prime necessarily to the first power.

sources.quote: **Claim FC-B1 (flat completeness).** ... `L(m)` is `1` or prime, and at most one prime factor of `m` exceeds `√m`

nodes.name: Algorithm C's Drain Is Incomplete for Factorization (FC1)
nodes.statement: There are composites m and primes p ∣ m with p² ≤ m that no layer of p claims, the least witness at W = 30 being m = 847 with p = 11, so C is a recursive rather than a flat factorizer.

sources.quote: **Claim FC1 (drain incompleteness of C).** There are composites `m` and primes `p ∣ m` with `p² ≤ m` such that no layer of `p` claims `m`.

nodes.name: Cofactor Chain Length (FC2)
nodes.statement: Iterating n ↦ n/spf(n)^{v} on a W-coprime n gives a strictly decreasing chain terminating at 1 of length at most log_{p_{w+1}} n, about 15 for n ≈ 10^18 with w = 6.

sources.quote: **Claim FC2 (chain length).** ... has length `≤ log_{p_{w+1}} n`

nodes.name: No Bounded Cofactor Window (FC3)
nodes.statement: The cofactors needed to factor every W-coprime n in [X, 2X) from Algorithm C's output are spread across [√X, 2X/p_{w+1}] and meet a positive proportion of the dyadic scales in between, so no bounded window suffices.
nodes.notes: Explicitly corrects min_factor.md §8 and its open problem 5.

sources.quote: **Claim FC3 (no bounded window).** ... spread across `[√X, 2X/p_{w+1}]`

nodes.name: Algorithm D — Flat Streaming Factorizer
nodes.statement: Algorithm D replaces Algorithm C's multiplier constraint r ≥ p by the cutoff p^e·r ≥ p², so every layer claims each of its multiples, and the drain plus one division for the large part reports the complete factorization of every candidate.

sources.heading: 6. Algorithm D
sources.quote: Replacing C's constraint `r ≥ p` with `p^e·r ≥ p²` yields Algorithm D

nodes.name: Algorithm D Claimant Identity (FC4)
nodes.statement: Layer (p, e) of Algorithm D claims m if and only if p ∣ m, e = v_p(m) and p² ≤ m, so claimants_D(m) is in bijection with claimants_B(m) but carries exponents.

sources.quote: **Claim FC4 (claimant identity).** ... a bijection onto `claimants_B(m)`.

nodes.name: Algorithm D Reports Complete Factorizations (FC5)
nodes.statement: The drain at m yields every (p, v_p(m)) with p ≤ √m and the residual L = m/∏p^{v_p} is 1 or a prime, so the full factorization is the drain plus one exact division.

sources.quote: **Claim FC5 (flat completeness).** ... the full factorization of `m` is the drain plus `L`.

nodes.name: Algorithm D Decision Rule (FC6)
nodes.statement: Every key in Algorithm D's queue is a W-coprime composite at least n and at least p²; a W-coprime candidate is prime exactly when no key equals it, and D emits exactly the primes forever.

sources.quote: **Claim FC6 (soundness, decision rule).** ... `D()` emits exactly the primes, forever.

nodes.name: Algorithm D Touches Equal Algorithm B's Exactly (FC7)
nodes.statement: ops_D(N) = ops_B(N) exactly, not merely to leading order, because the layers of a fixed p partition the W-coprime multiples of p in [p², N] by valuation.

sources.quote: **Claim FC7 (touch identity).** `ops_D(N) = ops_B(N)` **exactly**, not merely to leading order.

nodes.name: Correction M8′ — Smooth Numbers Are Not C-Layers
nodes.statement: The claim that y-smooth integers are a union of min-factor layers is false because smoothness is a condition on the largest prime factor while layers index the smallest; y-smooth integers are instead a union of truncated Algorithm A streams.

sources.quote: The smooth half is false. Smoothness is a condition on `P(m)`, and C indexes by `spf(m)`

nodes.name: Smooth Enumeration by Clamped Algorithm A (FC8)
nodes.statement: Running Algorithm A with every prime cursor clamped at y enumerates the y-smooth integers up to N in increasing order, one touch each, with live-stream count equal to the number of y-smooth bases b with b·P(b) ≤ N.
nodes.notes: Flagged in the notes as prior art: the Hamming-number heap generalised, superseded by Bernstein for counting.

sources.quote: **Claim FC8 (smooth enumeration).** Running Algorithm A with every prime cursor clamped at `y` enumerates the `y`-smooth integers `≤ N`

nodes.name: Ancestry Factorization in Algorithm A (FC9)
nodes.statement: Giving every Algorithm A base a parent pointer and label makes the multiset of prime factors of an emitted composite equal to its emission prime together with the labels on the path to the root, with no division and one touch per composite.

sources.quote: **Claim FC9 (ancestry).** ... the multiset of prime factors of `m` is `{q}` together with the labels on the path from `b` to the root

nodes.name: Orthogonal Stream Prime Generation
nodes.statement: Prime generation is a merge of pairwise disjoint composite streams, one per prime, each a prime times a wheel, requiring no marking array over the range and no divisibility test.

sources.heading: Abstract
sources.quote: each known prime `p` owns an infinite, strictly increasing _stream_ of composites ... the streams are pairwise disjoint

sources.heading: Abstract
sources.quote: Prime generation then reduces to a single sorted merge of pairwise disjoint composite streams

nodes.name: Generational Rings of Primes
nodes.statement: Primes are the exception points of an expanding periodic lattice: stage p certifies the band [p², p'²), each new prime breaks the current symmetry and immediately becomes a generator of the next, larger one.

sources.quote: each new prime is a break in the current periodic structure and simultaneously becomes a new generator that extends it

sources.heading: Why This Is Interesting
sources.quote: Each new prime is a break in the current symmetry, but it immediately becomes a fresh generator of the next, larger symmetry.

nodes.name: The Fractal (Moran/IFS) Reading
nodes.statement: The wheel lattices modulo the primorials form a Moran/IFS construction with non-constant contraction ratios 1/p_{k+1}, in which the set deleted at each stage is an affine copy of the previous stage and equals the stream Θ_p.

sources.heading: Overview
sources.quote: the lattice recursion is exact, and the set deleted at each stage is an _affine copy of the previous stage_
the stream decomposition and the fractal decomposition are the same theorem

nodes.name: Lattice Recursion (Claim F1)
nodes.statement: For p = p_{k+1}, S_{k+1} is the union of p translates of S_k modulo P_{k+1} minus the dilated copy p·S_k, and counting gives pφ(P_k) − φ(P_k) = φ(P_{k+1}).
nodes.notes: Routine (CRT + counting) but not yet formalised; its algorithmic content is machine-checked as theta_eq_image.

sources.quote: **Claim F1 (lattice recursion).** ... tile the previous lattice \(p\) times, then delete one dilated copy of it.
_Status: routine (CRT + counting); not yet formalised._

nodes.name: The Lattice Has Measure Zero and Box Dimension One (Claim F2)
nodes.statement: Rescaling stage k to [0,1] gives Lebesgue measure κ_k → 0 but box-counting dimension lim log φ(P_k)/log P_k = 1, so dimension is the wrong invariant for this construction.

sources.quote: the lattice is a **measure-zero, dimension-one** set: the fractality is real but _invisible to dimension_

nodes.name: The Sieve as a Stack of Orthogonal Periodic Fields
nodes.statement: The sieve is the pointwise product of per-prime periodic exclusion fields acting on independent CRT coordinates, which makes survivor density multiplicative, joint entropy additive and the finite Fourier decomposition prime-by-prime disjoint away from DC.

sources.heading: Abstract
sources.quote: a finite (and in the limit, infinite) product of orthogonal periodic exclusion fields, one per prime

sources.heading: What You Are Looking At
sources.quote: The sieve is the pointwise product of the individual masks.

nodes.name: Exact Periodicity of the Partial Sieve
nodes.statement: The product of the first k masks is exactly periodic with period L_k = P_k and has φ(P_k) survivors per period; this is not an asymptotic approximation but an exact repetition.

sources.quote: _the sieve is always exactly periodic, at every finite stage_, with a period that grows as the primorial

nodes.name: Survivor Density Is a Multiplicative Attenuation
nodes.statement: The survivor density after k primes is ρ_k = ∏_{i≤k}(1 − 1/p_i) with the exact recursion ρ_k = ρ_{k−1}(1 − 1/p_k), because each independent filter removes a fixed fraction of whatever survives.

sources.quote: each new prime removes a fixed fraction of _whatever survives so far_, regardless of the internal structure

nodes.name: Joint Entropy of the Per-Prime Indicators Is Additive
nodes.statement: Because the CRT coordinates are independent, the joint entropy of the k per-prime alive/dead indicators is exactly the sum of the marginals H(p_i), which must not be confused with the entropy of the one-bit sieve output.

sources.quote: the **joint entropy** of the \(k\) per-prime alive/dead indicators is exactly additive

nodes.name: Entropy Density Collapses; Per-Prime Increment Decays as log p / p
nodes.statement: The entropy per position h_k = H_joint(k)/L_k tends to zero rapidly because L_k grows primorially, and the marginal contribution of the k-th prime is H(p_k) ~ log p_k / p_k.

sources.quote: \Delta h_k = H(p_k) \sim \frac{\log p_k}{p_k}

nodes.name: CRT-Dual (Good–Thomas) Spectral Factorization
nodes.statement: Under the dual CRT indexing by tuples (m_1,…,m_k), the Fourier coefficient of the sieve factors as the product of the per-prime transforms, so multiplication in position space becomes convolution that stays cleanly separated by prime.

sources.quote: C_{(m_1,\ldots,m_k)} = \prod_{i=1}^k \hat M_{p_i}(m_i)

nodes.name: Disjoint Nonzero Spectral Support, Shared DC Term
nodes.statement: Each prime contributes a comb of nonzero harmonics at multiples of L/p with amplitude 1/p, and distinct primes occupy disjoint nonzero spectral support, but every prime contributes to the same DC coefficient (p−1)/p.
nodes.notes: idea.md explicitly corrects an earlier, stronger 'disjoint spectra' phrasing; the DC term is shared.

sources.quote: **disjoint nonzero spectral support**, not merely disjoint kill-sets in position space

nodes.name: The Limit Object Lives on the Profinite Integers
nodes.statement: Taking k → ∞ is grounded in the profinite integers Ẑ = lim Z/L_kZ with Haar measure, whose Pontryagin dual is Q/Z, so the prime spectrum is a function on rational frequencies rather than on a real frequency axis.

sources.quote: The natural ambient space is the **profinite integers** ... Its Pontryagin dual is the discrete group \(\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}\)

nodes.name: Zero-Entropy Odometer Obstruction to RH-Adjacent Readings
nodes.statement: The dynamical system underlying the construction is a zero-entropy equicontinuous profinite odometer, and Sarnak's Möbius disjointness conjecture asserts Möbius is orthogonal to all zero-entropy deterministic sequences, so this construction provably cannot capture the fine pseudorandomness of the primes.

sources.quote: there are principled dynamical reasons why this exact construction **cannot** capture the fine pseudorandomness of the primes

sources.heading: Honest Caveats
sources.quote: the underlying dynamical system is a zero-entropy profinite odometer

nodes.name: Wave–Particle Reading of Prime Gaps
nodes.statement: Primes are discrete irregular survivors in position space and pure periodic tones in frequency space, so a prime gap can be read as an interference pattern and a twin prime as a place where the small-prime waves fail to align.
nodes.notes: idea.md flags this as interpretive only, carrying no proof obligation and never usable as a premise.

sources.quote: Prime gaps, in this reading, are not primitive facts about primes; they are **interference patterns**

sources.heading: T56
sources.quote: Interpretive only. Carries no proof obligation and should never be used as a premise.

nodes.name: The Period–Window Dichotomy
nodes.statement: A wheel counts exactly over its full period P_k but certifies primality only on the window [p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}²), and the two ranges are separated by the doubly exponential factor p_{k+1}²/P_k = e^{−(1+o(1))p_k}.

sources.heading: 0. Summary
sources.quote: a wheel **counts exactly** over its full period `P_k`; a wheel **certifies primality** only on the window `[p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}²)`

nodes.name: One-Way Containment for Twin Candidates (TP0)
nodes.statement: The count of twin primes up to x with q > p_k is at most the count of positions whose residue lies in the pair lattice, with equality only on the window [p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}²−2).

sources.quote: **Claim TP0 (one-way containment).** ... Equality holds on `q ∈ [p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}² − 2)`

nodes.name: Pair Count Recursion T_{k+1} = (p−2)T_k (TP1)
nodes.statement: The number of twin-candidate residue classes satisfies T_1 = 1 and T_{k+1} = (p_{k+1} − 2)·T_k, so T_k = ∏_{3 ≤ p_i ≤ p_k}(p_i − 2), and the corresponding density obeys τ_{k+1} = τ_k(1 − 2/p).

sources.quote: **Claim TP1 (pair count).** `T_1 = 1` and, for `k ≥ 1` with `p = p_{k+1}`, `T_{k+1} = (p − 2)·T_k`.

nodes.name: Pair Lattice Promotion (TP2)
nodes.statement: Promotion replicates the pair lattice p times and deletes two disjoint dilated copies D and D' of shifted pair lattices, each of size T_k, so the deleted sets are affine images of a different member of the same family rather than of the stage itself.

sources.quote: **Claim TP2 (pair lattice recursion).** ... with `|D| = |D'| = T_k` and `D ∩ D' = ∅` for `p ≥ 3`

nodes.name: Pair Density Is the Hardy–Littlewood Singular Series (TP3)
nodes.statement: Exactly τ_k = ½·C_2(p_k)·∏_{3≤p≤p_k}(1 − 1/p)², and asymptotically τ_k ~ 2C_2 e^{−2γ}/log² p_k, so the pair lattice is the singular series materialised as a finite residue set.

sources.quote: The pair lattice therefore _is_ the Hardy–Littlewood singular series, materialised as a finite set of residues.

nodes.name: Hole Density Exceeds Prime Density by a Constant (TP3a)
nodes.statement: Sieving by all primes up to √x leaves survivor density 2e^{−γ}/log x against π(x)/x ~ 1/log x, and squaring gives the pair lattice a factor (2e^{−γ})² ≈ 1.26 above the conjectured twin density.

sources.quote: hole density is strictly larger than prime density, and the discrepancy does not vanish with `k`

nodes.name: Admissibility Criterion for Patterns (TP4)
nodes.statement: For a finite pattern H the class count is ∏_i(p_i − ν_i) with ν_i the number of residues of H mod p_i, and the class set is nonempty at every stage exactly when H is admissible.

sources.quote: **Claim TP4 (admissibility).** ... `S_k^{(H)} ≠ ∅` for all `k` iff `H` is admissible

nodes.name: Composite Pair-Holes Exist from Stage 4 (TP5)
nodes.statement: The pair lattice contains classes whose small representatives are composite in one or both coordinates as soon as p_{k+1}² < P_k, i.e. for k ≥ 4; examples are (167, 169) mod 210 and (527, 529) mod 2310.

nodes.name: Period-Wide Pair Counts Bound π_2 from Above (TP6)
nodes.statement: Because the containment of TP0 runs one way, growth of the twin-candidate count from stage to stage is growth of an upper bound and is compatible with π_2(x) being bounded.

sources.quote: **Claim TP6 (direction).** ... Growth of that count from stage to stage is growth of an upper bound

nodes.name: Pair Deletion Geometry (TP8)
nodes.statement: In the promotion the two deleted tiles of a class sit at j_0 = −rP̄ and j_1 = −(r+2)P̄ with fixed difference δ_k ≡ −2P̄ independent of the class, so no copy is deleted twice, D' = D + δ_k·P is a rigid translate of D, and survivors form two cyclic arcs with a run of at least ⌈(p−2)/2⌉ consecutive copies.

sources.quote: **Claim TP8 (deletion geometry).** ... `j_1(r) − j_0(r) ≡ −2P̄ =: δ_k (mod p)`, **independent of `r`**

nodes.name: Deleted Copies Are Adjacent Iff P_k ≡ ∓2 (TP8a)
nodes.statement: The two deleted copies of a class are cyclically adjacent exactly when δ_k ≡ ±1 mod p_{k+1}, i.e. when P_k ≡ ∓2 mod p_{k+1}; this occurs at k = 3, where mod 210 every class loses copies j = 4 and j = 5.

sources.quote: **Remark TP8a (adjacency criterion).** The two deleted copies of a class are cyclically **adjacent** exactly when `δ_k ≡ ±1 (mod p)`

nodes.name: Window Occupancy (Claim W)
nodes.statement: For every prime p > 2 there exists h with p ≤ h, h + 2 < p², and both h and h+2 p-rough, i.e. the pair lattice below p has a hole-pair inside the certified window.

sources.quote: **Claim W (window occupancy).** For every prime `p > 2` there exist `h` with `p ≤ h`, `h + 2 < p²`
the unrestricted form is outright false (`Twin.not_windowAt_two`)

nodes.name: Window Occupancy Implies the Twin Prime Conjecture (TP7)
nodes.statement: Claim W implies there are infinitely many twin primes, by applying phase separation to both coordinates of the window witness; the machine-checked proof cites only prime_of_rough_of_lt_sq and never mentions the promotion recursion.

sources.quote: **Claim TP7 (W ⟹ TPC).** Claim W implies there are infinitely many twin primes.

nodes.name: Pair Jacobsthal Bound (TP-J)
nodes.statement: The maximal gap g_2(P_k) between consecutive elements of the pair lattice satisfies g_2(P_k) ≪ log² P_k ≍ p_k², which would imply Claim W and hence the twin prime conjecture.

sources.quote: **Conjecture TP-J (pair Jacobsthal).** `g_2(P_k) ≪ log² P_k ≍ p_k²`.

nodes.name: Window Occupancy Verified for Every Prime Below 60
nodes.statement: Enumerating window witnesses for every prime below 60 gives at least two hole-pairs at each prime above 2 and none at 2, with observed-to-predicted occupancy ratios in the range 0.66 to 1.19 and no visible trend.

sources.quote: **W holds for every prime `2 < p < 60`**, with the witness count never below `2`.

nodes.name: Twin Generator on Top of Algorithm B
nodes.statement: Twin detection costs one register on top of Algorithm B: remember the previous emitted prime and emit the pair when the difference is 2, inheriting O(π(√n)) memory and O(1) random-access restart.

sources.quote: Twin detection is one register ... No extra asymptotic cost

nodes.name: Pair Wheel for the Scan
nodes.statement: Restricting the scan to pair-spokes tests only 25.8% of spoke positions at W = 30030, a 3.88× reduction; the saving applies to the scan only, because pair-restricting the advance would need a per-prime table and hence primorial space.

sources.quote: pair-restrict the scan, never the advance

nodes.name: Bucket Priority Queue Engineering Layer
nodes.statement: Replacing the binary heap by per-segment bucket lists plus a Δ-bit mark array makes every queue operation O(1) amortised and sequential in memory, at the cost of reintroducing a segment-sized array.

sources.quote: All operations are O(1) amortised and sequential in memory.
This reintroduces a _segment-sized_ array

nodes.name: Wheel Density Returns Are Doubly Logarithmic
nodes.statement: w = 6 gives κ = 0.1918 at W = 30030 while w = 8 gives κ = 0.1636 at W = 9699690 — a 323× larger table for 15% fewer touches — and halving κ to about 0.10 would require a modulus of order 10^117.

sources.quote: a 323× larger table for 15% fewer touches — and _halving_ `κ` to ≈ 0.10 requires primes up to ≈ 274

nodes.name: 121 Is a Composite Hole Inside the Mod-210 Wheel's First Period
nodes.statement: 121 = 11² is coprime to 210 and smaller than 210, so the mod-210 lattice already contains a composite hole within its own first period; for k ≤ 3 no such hole exists.

sources.quote: \(121 = 11^2 \in S_4\) ... so the mod-210 lattice has a composite hole inside its first period

nodes.name: Python Reference Implementation (primes_A, primes_B, primes_C)
nodes.statement: algorithm.md §6 contains an executable, self-checking Python reference implementing the wheel tables, Algorithm A with statistics, Algorithm B and Algorithm C with min-factor reporting, validated against a sieve to 200,000.

sources.quote: ## 6. Reference implementation (Python, executable and self-checking)

nodes.name: Lean 4 / Mathlib Formalisation
nodes.statement: The directory lean/ contains a sorry-free Lean 4 + Mathlib formalisation of the structural claims — ownership, phase separation, causality, the wheel successor spec, the stream tree, and Algorithm B's coverage, soundness, invariant and claimant set.

sources.quote: `lean/` contains a `sorry`-free Lean 4 + Mathlib formalisation of the structural claims

nodes.name: lean/Primegen/Twin.lean
nodes.statement: Twin.lean is sorry-free and contains kernel-checked fragments of the twin material: TP7 in full, TP0's rough half, TP1's per-prime factor, TP8(a) and (b), and the statement of Claim W with witnesses for small primes.

sources.quote: `lean/Primegen/Twin.lean` is `sorry`-free and builds against the pinned Mathlib.

nodes.name: pops == composites Assertion for Algorithm A
nodes.statement: Running primes_A with statistics and asserting that the pop count equals the composite count is a machine-checkable certificate of exact orthogonality that fails immediately if any composite is claimed twice or missed.

sources.quote: The assertion `pops == composites` is the machine-checkable statement of exact orthogonality (Theorem 3.2)

nodes.name: Measure S(N) and Fit the Exponent θ
nodes.statement: Sharp asymptotics for S(N) = #{ b ≥ 2 : b·P(b) ≤ N }, the memory of Algorithm A, are unknown; the peak queue size reported by the reference implementation should be used to fit θ rather than trusting the heuristic exponent.

sources.quote: Sharp asymptotics for \(S(N) = \#\{b\ge2 : b\,P(b)\le N\}\) — the memory of Algorithm A.

nodes.name: Optimal Wheel Index w as a Function of N and Cache
nodes.statement: The best choice of w trades the density κ_W and the ln ln span against the Θ(W)-byte table and cache behaviour, and the optimum as a function of N and cache size is not determined.

sources.quote: Optimal \(w\) as a function of \(N\) and cache size for Algorithm B

nodes.name: Hybrid of A's Exact Streams and B's Prime Phase
nodes.statement: Running Algorithm A's exact streams for p ≤ N^{1/3} and Algorithm B's index-increment prime phase above should give one-touch behaviour with a much smaller S(N), but the accounting has not been done.

sources.quote: This should get one-touch behaviour with much smaller \(S(N)\); the accounting is not yet done.

nodes.name: Formalise the Outer Induction for Algorithm B
nodes.statement: The statement that the list emitted by Algorithm B is exactly the primes below n is not formalised; the per-candidate decision and invariant preservation are done, and wiring them into a loop invariant needs the self-hosting argument.

sources.quote: **The outer induction.** Formalise "the list emitted by `B()` is exactly the primes below `n`".

nodes.name: Exponent-Spine Algorithm A
nodes.statement: Indexing Algorithm A's bases as b = p^e·b' and run-length encoding the spine may suppress the smooth bases that dominate S(N), as the wheel variant does, but this has not been analysed.

sources.quote: **Exponent-spine Algorithm A:** index A's bases as \(b = p^{e}b'\) and run-length encode the spine.

nodes.name: The Bicone Index (spf, v_spf, P(m))
nodes.statement: Indexing composites simultaneously by the min-factor spine and the largest prime factor would give one traversal that is a smoothness oracle, a roughness oracle and a complete factorizer with segment restart, if the live-stream count is only polylog above π(√N).

sources.quote: **The bicone index (§7.3).** Index composites by `(spf, v_spf, P(m))`

nodes.name: Does Any Log-Periodicity Survive the Non-Constant Ratios?
nodes.statement: Because the Moran ratios 1/p_k are non-constant and unbounded, no exact scaling symmetry survives; whether any approximate log-periodicity appears in prime statistics at primorial scales must be measured rather than asserted.

sources.quote: Does any _approximate_ log-periodicity show up in prime statistics at primorial scales, or is the apparent signal an artefact of binning?

nodes.name: Sharp φ(P_k) → π Transfer in the Certified Window
nodes.statement: A sharp form of the transfer from wheel survivors to primes in the window [p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}²) — Buchstab's ω made effective — is open and is the only place in the construction where genuinely non-trivial fluctuation lives.

sources.quote: **The `φ(P_k) → π` transfer.** Sharp form of the transfer in the certified window

nodes.name: Measure the Pair Jacobsthal Function g_2(P_k)
nodes.statement: Computing g_2(P_k) exactly for k ≤ 8 and by segmented enumeration for k ≤ 12, then fitting g_2(P_k) ≍ p_k^α, is the single most informative experiment the framework supports for the twin question.

sources.quote: **Measure `g_2(P_k)`** exactly for `k ≤ 8` and by segmented enumeration for `k ≤ 12`

nodes.name: Measure ops_C Against ops_B and Fit the N^{2/3} Gap
nodes.statement: The claimed Θ(N^{2/3}/log N) gap between Algorithm C's and Algorithm B's touch counts should be measured at N = 10^8 … 10^12 with pop counters, along with the thinned-spine record count against π(√N).
